promptSegments.text: Yasmin ______ my cousin, and ______ favourite hobby is art.

feedback.explanation: Use is with the singular subject Yasmin. Her is the possessive adjective before favourite hobby.

promptSegments.text: These are ______ notebooks, but ______ pencil is mine.

feedback.explanation: Farah's shows possession. This refers to one nearby pencil.

promptSegments.text: ______ you got a camera in your bag?

feedback.explanation: Use Have you got to ask whether someone possesses something.

promptSegments.text: ______ any parks near your house?

feedback.explanation: Parks is plural, so a question about their existence begins Are there.

promptSegments.text: This park is ______ than the one near my home.

feedback.explanation: Than compares two parks. The usual comparative form of quiet is quieter.

promptSegments.text: My brother ______ to school by bus every day.

feedback.explanation: Every day describes a habit. With the singular subject my brother, use goes.

promptSegments.text: My father ______ drive to work, but he ______ the bus every morning.

feedback.explanation: With he, use doesn't before the base verb drive. In the positive present simple, use he takes.

promptSegments.text: The blue whale is ______ animal in the world.

feedback.explanation: Use the before the superlative: the largest animal in the world.

promptSegments.text: My sister ______ swim well, but my little brother ______ swim yet.

feedback.explanation: Can expresses ability. Can't expresses that the little brother is not able to swim yet.

promptSegments.text: ______ the children ______ in the hall right now?

feedback.explanation: Right now calls for the present continuous. Children is plural, so use Are the children dancing?

promptSegments.text: Hana usually ______ in the library, but today she ______ at home.

feedback.explanation: Usually describes a habit, so use studies. Today describes a temporary current activity, so use is studying.

promptSegments.text: How ______ water do we need, and how ______ apples should we buy?

feedback.explanation: Water is uncountable, so use much. Apples are countable and plural, so use many.

promptSegments.text: My sister enjoys ______, so please ______ some vegetables for dinner.

feedback.explanation: Enjoys is followed by an -ing form: cooking. After please, use the base verb wash.

promptSegments.text: There ______ many spectators at the stadium, but there ______ only one winner.

feedback.explanation: Use were with the plural spectators and was with the singular one winner.

promptSegments.text: He ______ a gold medal after he ______ the race last year.

feedback.explanation: Last year refers to completed past events, so use the past simple forms won and finished.

promptSegments.text: I saw Aina yesterday, but I didn't ______ to ______.

feedback.explanation: After didn't, use the base verb talk. After the preposition to, use the object pronoun her.

promptSegments.text: ______ you ______ the football match last Sunday?

feedback.explanation: Last Sunday requires a past-tense question. After Did, use the base verb watch.

promptSegments.text: They ______ travel to Sabah next month; the tickets are already booked.

feedback.explanation: The tickets show a future plan. With the plural subject they, use are going to.

promptSegments.text: I think the Tigers ______ win tomorrow's match.

feedback.explanation: I think introduces a prediction about tomorrow, so use will win.

promptSegments.text: Your bag looks heavy; I ______ carry it for you.

feedback.explanation: Will expresses a spontaneous offer made at the moment of speaking.
